title: Paloma Business Account Terms: Accounts per Owner and per Business
content:
**Clause 1. Accounts an owner may administer.** One owner may administer up to 3 Paloma Business accounts, each for a different legal business.

**Clause 2. One account per business.** A business may hold only one Paloma Business account. An application is accepted only when no other Paloma Business account whose status is anything other than closed carries the same last four digits of the EIN and the same legal business name.

**Clause 3. No second account for more allowance.** An application is never a second account for the same business to obtain a second allowance or volume limit; a business that wants more moves to a higher plan.

### How the duplicate test is read

| Element | What the test looks at |
|---|---|
| Evidence | The Paloma Business account records, checked before the application is accepted |
| Object | The business, identified by the last four digits of its EIN and its legal business name, taken together |
| Accounts that block an application | Any other Paloma Business account with that same pair whose status is pending KYB, active, past due or suspended |
| Accounts that do not block it | A Paloma Business account with that same pair whose status is closed |

### Cases (hypothetical)

1. An earlier Paloma Business account carrying the same EIN last four digits and the same legal business name is **active**. Under Clause 2 the new application is not accepted.
2. The only earlier Paloma Business account carrying the same pair is **closed**. Clause 2 does not stand in the way of the new application.
3. An owner already administers 3 Paloma Business accounts for 3 different legal businesses and applies for a further account for a fourth business. Clause 1 allows up to 3, so the fourth is beyond what one owner may administer.
4. A business on one plan wants a larger free payout allowance and volume limit. Clause 3 rules out a second account for that purpose; the business moves to a higher plan.
